isolation: SEARCH copies search.py into a synthetic temporary repo with a local stub router, synthetic credential files, synthetic digests and a synthetic index.
SEARCH provider stub blocks socket.socket.connect and socket.create_connection and returns synthetic vectors or synthetic exceptions.
SEARCH build/query invocations run only the copied fixture script. The production CLI is never invoked.
DIGEST injects fake exec, runOneShot, notify and log implementations; commands are mocked and digest writes stay in temporary repos.
No installs, live provider calls, real credentials, real transcripts, real index access, app startup, scheduler activation or restarts.
limitations: SEARCH uses a stub router and DIGEST mocks subprocess calls; neither test suite exercises the candidate wheel or proves shared-install compatibility.
No live provider behavior, installed app activation, production index rebuild or scheduler integration is established.
SEARCH network blocking is supplied by the reviewed provider stub, not an operating-system firewall.
Outer synthetic temporary directories are preserved; SEARCH performs its existing internal fixture cleanup.
prior_attempt: Identical sanitized suites returned exit 0; repeated only because Windows did not forward child stdout without explicit redirection.
